label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Renee, I am Thu, the owner of Lotus Garden Nails. I am truly sorry that your toe became painful and swollen, and that you had to go to urgent care, take antibiotics, and could not wear shoes comfortably for a week. I mean that sincerely. You have been my customer for two years, and I do not want to fight with you on this forum. But because my salon and my niece have been discussed publicly, I would like to explain our side calmly.

You came in on Saturday, October 24, for a $45 deluxe pedicure. Your technician was my niece Vy, who has been a licensed nail technician for three years. All reusable metal implements at my salon are sterilized in an autoclave and kept in a sealed pouch, which we open in front of the customer. Files and buffers are new for each person, and the customer can take them home. We also put a fresh plastic liner in the pedicure tub for every service.

When you came back on November 2 and showed me your red toe, I am sorry if you felt that I shrugged at you or did not care. That was not my intention. I offered you the full $45 refund and also offered to pay your urgent-care copay if you brought me the receipt. You also asked for $300 cash and free pedicures for one year. I said no to that request, but I did not refuse to offer any help.

There is one part of the pedicure that I need to clarify. Vy told me that during the service, you asked her several times to trim the cuticle more because you wanted it very clean. She told you she did not want to cut too much, and you told her it was fine because you always did it that way. I am not saying this to blame you for your toe hurting. I am not a doctor, and I cannot determine online what caused your infection. I only want the conversation between you and Vy to be described accurately.

I also need to say that describing Vy as someone who barely speaks English is not fair to her. Vy was born in Houston and speaks English. She is shy, especially when a customer is unhappy, but being shy is not the same as being unable to communicate. She read these posts and cried, and she even told me she wanted to quit doing nails. She cares about her work, and it hurts me to see her professionalism judged this way.

My salon passed its state inspection in August 2026 with no violations. The inspection paper is posted on the wall. Renee, you said you have filed with the state, and of course I will cooperate fully.

I opened Lotus Garden in 2007 after working for my aunt, and this is my 19th year in Houston. In all that time, no customer has ever brought me an infection complaint before. That does not mean your pain is not real. It means I take this very seriously. What has hurt me most is reading people say that all these small nail salons are dirty, reuse files, or have nasty tubs, as if we are all the same. Please judge my salon by what we actually do.

Marisol, thank you for speaking kindly about your own experience and for suggesting that Renee talk with me again, without dismissing what she went through. I appreciate that very much.

Renee, my offer is still open: the full $45 refund and payment of your urgent-care copay when you bring the receipt. Please call the salon or come in and ask for me so we can talk calmly and privately. I would much rather speak with you directly than continue back and forth here. I hope your toe heals completely and quickly.
